title: Every Demo Video Gets a Home, and a YouTube Queue | vitalii.no
description:
Every time I finished a polished product-demo video, it had nowhere real to go — just a local mp4 file I'd eventually drop into a YouTube upload by hand. There was no public catalog page per project, no way to keep an older cut around next to a newer one, and no link between a finished render and the daily queue that already handles feature clips.

I built a Cloudflare Worker (site/src/index.js) backed by one R2 bucket that stores every project's demo videos plus a catalog describing all projects and versions. scripts/demo.mjs is the CLI: a single publish command uploads the file and registers the version, while list, hide, show and delete manage visibility. A systemd timer polls every 15 minutes and feeds pending versions into the same queue that already uploads feature clips, then marks the version live and adds it to the 'Product demos — vitalii.no' playlist.

demo-video.vitalii.no is now live with a working publish-to-YouTube pipeline: one command handles both the site catalog and the shared queue, and the upload path enforces the real 95 megabyte limit instead of failing silently on oversized files.
